AH01.title: First run - a hive with assets but no reliability work
AH01.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. GROUND first: there was no cold-start asset to walk. Measured 79 approved nodes and 0 of them lacked a Weibull fit - reliability.py fitted EVERY node unconditionally - so the state every newly-commissioned machine, and every new customer's entire fleet on day one, had never once been rendered. Built one (COLD-001) and made it reproducible in the seeder (~12% of nodes left with no FMEA, no fit, no P-F - all four skipped TOGETHER, since an asset with an FMEA but no fit is a different, already-covered state). Gate extended: asset_nodes.cold_start, now 7 states held open. WHAT HELD UP on a genuinely cold asset: all three Workbench empty states render with an actionable next step; the risk board says a score is computed daily at 13:00 PHT rather than showing a zero; and the Print Report is honest section by section - 'No approved FMEA modes registered', 'No Weibull fit yet. Compute on the Weibull tab once at least 4 corrective events are logged', 'No P-F intervals computed' - each naming the tab to go to. That is a good cold start. TWO DEFECTS FOUND. (1) TELEMETRY: the card hid itself whenever an asset had no readings, which made #telemetry-empty DEAD CODE - the only branch that could show it hid its parent instead. It collapsed two different situations into one silence: 'this hive has no bridge' (hiding is right) and 'the bridge is up, this asset is unmapped' (silence is a wrong answer). Measured 17 of 79 assets carry readings, so 62 sat silent on hives that plainly do have a bridge. Now hive-scoped: hide only when the hive has no telemetry at all, otherwise say which one it is. (2) DEEP-LINK: the ?node_id= branch had NO else - an unresolvable id dropped the user into the full unfiltered fleet with no explanation. This is EXACTLY the failure the ?tag= arm was fixed for in §12 JA1/JA2 on 2026-07-23; the fix went to one arm of the same if/else and not the other. Not an edge case: the fleet list is approved-only, so EVERY pending or rejected asset is unresolvable - 17 of 96 nodes, ~18% - and a supervisor following a link to a submission they were asked to review could not tell their target had been missed. Fixed to name the asset and its actual state and scroll to Pending Approvals. Deliberately NOT forcing the detail open for a non-approved node: openDetail and ~10 downstream renderers all resolve from _allNodes and would each render a blank. A RACE FOUND WHILE VERIFYING IT: loadPendingAssets() was fire-and-forget, so the deep-link resolved against an empty _pendingNodes and a genuinely-pending asset reported 'could not be resolved' - the node was in the queue 2s later. Now awaited. All four arrivals verified live: approved -> detail opens; pending -> 'CR-001 is still awaiting approval... see Pending Approvals' + card scrolled to top; rejected -> 'GEN-004 was rejected...'; bogus uuid -> 'That asset link could not be resolved in this hive.' INSTRUMENT ERROR EN ROUTE, twice worth recording: I first probed v_sensor_recent with a quality_flag column copied from v_sensor_truth and read the 42703 as evidence about the page; and I polled for toasts with [class*=toast] when the element is id=toast with NO class, so two correct fixes read as silent failures. Verify the instrument before believing the page.

AH02.title: Worker submits an asset -> it enters the pending queue
AH02.notes: FIXTURE BUILT, THEN WALKED 2026-07-28. The blocker was real and it was in the SEEDER hand-off: assets.py computes auth_uid from the submitter but builds ctx in memory only, and asset_brain.py - which does the actual asset_nodes insert - DROPPED auth_uid from its row mapping and hardcoded status='approved'. Two omissions, and between them the page's whole governance workflow was untestable: 95 rows, 0 with an author, 0 pending, 0 rejected. Fixed at the source (_governance_state generates the status and its companion fields TOGETHER so a pending row cannot claim a reviewer and a rejected row cannot lack a reason - the PM9 coherence lesson), and auth_uid is now carried through. Verified over 400 draws: 82/12/6 approved/pending/rejected, ZERO internally inconsistent rows. Applied to the live fixture too: 79 approved / 12 pending / 4 rejected, authors attached (5 approved rows keep no author because they had no submitted_by to resolve - recorded, not hidden).

AH03.title: Supervisor approves / rejects - and the rejection must SAY WHY
AH03.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28 and found a REAL authority hole - the first thing the new fixture made visible. THE GOOD HALF FIRST: wh_guard_supervisor_approval is a well-built generic trigger (SECURITY DEFINER, six tables, service_role exempt) and it correctly refuses a non-supervisor who APPROVES - a worker approving their own pending asset is rejected 42501 with a message naming the user and hive. That is the opposite of the PM arc's pattern and stays exactly as it is. THE HOLE: its UPDATE clause treated a status change as privileged only when 'approved' was on one side, so pending -> rejected slipped through. ('rejected' does appear in sup_states, but that array is only consulted for the wo_state column.) Probed live: a WORKER set their own pending asset to 'rejected' AND wrote rejection_reason = 'Rejected by the supervisor - not fit for the register.' One row, no error. REACHABLE, not theoretical: asset-hub's own reject is caught only INCIDENTALLY, because it also writes approved_by/approved_at and the guard notices those. hive.html's rejectItem() updates { status: 'rejected' } ALONE, behind a client-side role check - PMK6's class on the approval queue. WHY THE REASON FIELD IS THE SHARP PART: rejection_reason is the REVIEWER'S VOICE. The queue renders it back to the submitter as 'Why: ...' and the PDDA arc added it precisely so a rejection would explain itself. A submitter who can write it authors a verdict in a supervisor's name, and the next supervisor reading the queue cannot tell. FIXED centrally in migration 20260728000013 - one clause, SIX tables, because every approval queue on the platform shared the hole. Safe to tighten, measured first: both legitimate reject paths are already supervisor-only in their UI and service_role is exempt. Proven: worker self-reject BLOCKED, worker editing the reason alone BLOCKED, supervisor reject still 1 row. GATED by tools/validate_approval_authority.py (registered); teeth proven against the REAL pre-fix guard - 3 of 4 checks fail, exit 1.

AH04.title: Restore a rejected asset - can the submitter see what happened?
AH04.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28, and it closes the loop the whole arc has been circling. The queue that holds rejection_reason was loaded ONLY for supervisors (`if (HIVE_ROLE === 'supervisor') loadPendingAssets()`), which is the inherited PDDA finding F21 - but F21 undersold it. It is not just that a worker's Pending tile reads 0: rejection_reason is the sentence a reviewer writes FOR THE SUBMITTER, rendered as 'Why: ...', and it was shown to everyone EXCEPT the person it was addressed to. Measured: 6 worker-submitted pending and 3 rejected, all 3 carrying a reason, none visible to the 3 people who wrote the submissions. So this arc secured that field (AH3 - a submitter could forge it), recorded the decision behind it (AHK1 - 83 decisions, 0 records), and the reader it exists for could not see it. FIXED: the queue loads for everyone, and the QUERY is scoped by role - a supervisor reviews the hive's queue, anyone else sees only rows they authored. Scoped on auth_uid rather than worker_name, because the name is display text while the uid is the identity bind_asset_nodes_submitter bound on insert. The reviewer BUTTONS stay supervisor-only; a submitter sees their standing instead ('Waiting for a supervisor to review this.' / 'Rejected - edit and resubmit, or ask your supervisor.'). VERIFIED BOTH SIDES. With submissions: running the page's exact new query as Ricardo Morales (worker) returns 3 of HIS OWN rows rather than the hive-wide 6, and he can now read 'Duplicate of an existing tag - please check the fleet list first.' Without submissions: as Christine Dizon (worker, none) the card stays hidden, 0 rows, page alive - no crash and no empty card shouting at her.

AH05.title: Fleet list: search, 200-row cap, QR scan (inherited F20)
AH05.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28 - the inherited F20, and the page turned out to be MOSTLY right already, which is worth recording precisely so the next reader does not re-open it. The summary tiles do NOT derive from the capped list: _assetTotalCount / _assetCriticalCount come from their own uncapped count queries, with a comment explaining exactly why. And the visible list is progressively paginated client-side with an honest 'showing N of M'. Both halves were already handled. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY SILENT is the SERVER cap beneath all of that: the fleet query is .limit(200), so a hive with more approved assets gets a list quietly missing the rest WHILE the tiles keep reporting the true total. The two would disagree and nothing would explain why - the reader would have to guess whether the fleet or the tile was wrong. LATENT, NOT LIVE: the largest hive holds 35 assets, so no customer has hit it. Recorded and closed anyway rather than left for the first customer big enough to find it - the same disposition as PM8's ELSE-30. FIXED with a note that appears ONLY when the cap actually truncates (_allNodes.length >= 200 AND the true total exceeds it), reserved in the markup so revealing it cannot shift the list. Logic proven over five cases including the null-total and exactly-200 boundaries; verified live both ways - hidden at the real 29-asset scale, and reading 'Showing the first 200 assets of 247. Search to narrow the list.' when simulated at the cap. AN INSTRUMENT ERROR EN ROUTE: my first simulation set window._assetTotalCount, but that binding is a top-level `let` and never lands on window, so the closure kept reading the real value and the note correctly stayed hidden - which I nearly misread as the fix not working. Assigning the binding directly proved it.

AH06.title: Asset detail - the 11-view roll-up renders honestly per state
AH06.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. Counted all 11 truth views the page reads, live, as the signed-in user: v_asset_truth 30 (approved-only, matching the fleet list), v_fmea_truth 77, v_logbook_truth 1171, v_marketplace_listings_truth 8, v_pf_truth 31, v_rcm_truth 50, v_risk_truth 9, v_sensor_recent 19029, v_sensor_truth 18, v_weibull_truth 35 - and v_external_sync_truth ZERO. external_sync held 0 rows PLATFORM-WIDE while the page read that view to render 'Last synced from SAP PM 3 days ago' beneath the CMMS-id card. An empty table feeding a live UI element is the AHK3 class again, and it is the OTHER HALF of the inherited F18 dead card: AH17 gave the card its ids, and the ids still had no provenance. Nothing looked broken - the line was simply always blank. WORSE THAN BLANK, IT WAS AMBIGUOUS: the same empty string answered 'the lookup errored' and 'this id has never been synced', and the second is the one that matters. An asset carrying SAP_PM: EQ-GEN002 with no sync record means the id was typed in or imported once and nothing has confirmed it since - exactly what an engineer needs to know BEFORE trusting it to raise a work order in the other system. Now says so. AND A FAILING INTEGRATION READ THE SAME AS A HEALTHY ONE: 'synced 2h ago (active)' and 'broken for 30 days (error)' were the same muted grey, distinguished only by a word in parentheses. The error state now says what it MEANS ('Sync from SAP_PM is FAILING - last contact 1d ago. These ids may no longer match the source system.') in red at weight 600 - and the WORDING carries the signal too, not just the colour, so it survives greyscale printing and anyone who cannot separate the hue. ONE MORE LABEL CORRECTED BEFORE IT SHIPPED: my first wording said 'last SUCCESSFUL contact', but last_synced_at records when the sync last RAN, and on an error row that run is precisely the one that failed. Calling it a success would have been the label claiming what the column does not support - the same class as AH16's '500 readings in the last 30 days'. Seeder now produces the populated state (with an error sample, because a FAILING sync is what a planner most needs to see and a happy-path fixture never generates it), and both states verified live: RC-002 'Last synced from Fiix at 2d ago (active)', PB-001 'No sync on record for these ids', SUB-001 the red FAILING line. The other ten views were already honest per state, which the AH1/AH7/AH16 walks had exercised between them: the Workbench empty states, the risk board's 'computed daily at 13:00 PHT', the report's section-by-section refusals, and the telemetry card's two distinct silences.

AH07.title: FMEA: add a failure mode, RPN is computed and defensible
AH07.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. The arithmetic was NOT the problem and it is worth saying so precisely: rpn is a GENERATED ALWAYS column (COALESCE(severity,0) * COALESCE(occurrence,0) * COALESCE(detection,0)), so it cannot drift from its inputs - 0 of 300 rows disagree - and severity, occurrence and detection are each CHECK-bounded 1..10, with consequence_class bounded to a fixed set. The inputs are defensible. THE DEFECT IS WHAT THE PAGE DOES WITH THEM. Every FMEA surface ordered by rpn DESC alone, and RPN multiplies severity by how RARE and how DETECTABLE a failure is - so a rare, easily-caught SAFETY failure scores below a frequent, hard-to-spot nuisance. MEASURED: all 17 modes with severity >= 9 fall below the median RPN, and on WLD-001 'Cable insulation breakdown' (S9, consequence_class=safety, RPN 108) ranked BELOW 'MCCB trip unit drift' (S8, RPN 168) and 'Switch-mode PSU output ripple' (S5, production, RPN 150). Fleet-wide the worst case is that same S9 safety mode sitting under 'Coupling misalignment beyond 0.05 mm' (S6, production, RPN 180). The electrocution risk sat under the alignment nuisance on every asset page and every printed report. AND WE HAD ALREADY WRITTEN THE CAVEAT DOWN. canonical/standards.json iec_60812_2018.rpn says 'Newer guidance (AIAG-VDA 2019) favours Action Priority over RPN' - and the Print Report's own section header reads '1. FMEA matrix (AIAG-VDA 2019)', citing the standard that replaced RPN because of exactly this, while the table under it was in RPN order. Documented the weakness, then shipped it. FIX: an Action Priority band (_fmeaActionPriority / _fmeaPriorityOrder) - H when severity >= 9 (safety or regulatory consequence, regardless of how rare or detectable) or RPN >= 200; M when severity >= 7 or RPN >= 100; L otherwise; ordered by band then RPN within a band. It only ever RAISES priority: the RPN colour banding is untouched, so nothing that reads as urgent today is quietly demoted - the safety item simply stops being buried under it. The pill carries WHY in its title so an engineer who wonders why a mid-RPN row is on top gets the reason without leaving the page. HONEST SCOPE, and this is the part that mattered most to get right: this is NOT the full AIAG-VDA AP lookup, which is a ~1000-cell S/O/D table. I did not reproduce it, because inventing a standard's table contents would defeat the entire point of an auditable contract - the surfaces say AP and cite the standards rather than claiming full AIAG-VDA conformance, and the formula is registered with partial_variant=true and a partial_reason that says exactly this. What IS implemented is the severity escalation both IEC 60812:2018 and AIAG-VDA agree on, which is what fixes the measured burial. BOTH SURFACES, one order: the printed report goes through the same function as the screen, because an auditor and an engineer disagreeing about which failure matters most would be worse than the original bug. Report also gained an AP column, 'highest severity' and 'N at Action Priority H' in the executive summary, and a sentence explaining why the table is not in RPN order. VERIFIED LIVE on WLD-001: the S9 safety mode now renders first (AP H, RPN 108) above the RPN 168 and 150, and the generated report table matches row for row. GATE validate_fmea_priority_order, teeth proven TWICE: reverting the report to rpn order -> FAIL; dropping the severity CHECK -> FAIL. Its live half deliberately does NOT sort by its own rule and then assert its own rule holds - that tautology can never fail - it checks the substrate the bands stand on (rpn still generated, S/O/D still bounded 1..10) and reports the 17-mode burial count so the reason for the rule stays visible instead of becoming folklore.

AH08.title: RCM strategy -> interval -> push to PM Scheduler
AH08.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28, after building the TWO fixture states it needed - and the fixture work is the finding. (1) rcm_strategies was 172 approved / 0 unapproved, because reliability.py set approved_by/approved_at UNCONDITIONALLY while the fmea_modes rows twelve lines above already had an is_approved branch (245 of 300). Same file, adjacent tables, one walkable and one not. It matters because pushStrategyToPm() refuses an unapproved strategy - 'Strategy must be approved before pushing to PM Scheduler' - so with no unapproved rows in existence that REFUSAL had never once been exercised; the guard could have been inverted or dead and nothing would have shown it. Fixed to mirror the FMEA branch, coherently (an unapproved strategy has NEITHER an approver nor a timestamp). Live: 146 approved / 26 unapproved. (2) 0 of 172 strategies were linked to a PM scope item. RECALLING THE DISPOSITION stopped this being filed as a bug: the seeder comment calls the unlinked state 'the realistic cold-start state', and that is right. But with EVERY row cold-start the linked branch was undemonstrable - pushStrategyToPm's idempotence guard ('Already linked to PM Scheduler') and the written_to_pm_scope_item_id FK had no row to protect. That is the logbook arc's LB13 exactly. Resolved the same way: seed a SAMPLE so BOTH branches exist without pretending every plant has finished its RCM roll-out. Live: 21 of 172 linked, 0 dangling. THE CORRECTNESS RESULT: no pushed scope item is scheduled RARER than its strategy specifies (0 of 21), none sits in a different hive from its strategy, and the pairs are exact - 30d->Monthly, 90d->Quarterly, 180d->Semi-Annual. That property does not rest on the fixture: only 3 distinct intervals exist in the data (30/90/180, all canonical buckets), so the mapping is barely exercised here - it holds for ARBITRARY intervals because validate_pm_frequency_mapping proves never-rarer across 1..400, the PMK4 gate from the PM arc. A MISTAKE OF MY OWN, caught and undone: my first bulk link paired rows by two unrelated row_number() orderings, so 18 of 21 strategies got ANOTHER strategy's scope item (a 30-day strategy pointing at a Semi-Annual task). Caught by verifying the pairing rather than the row count, fully reverted (links cleared, the 21 wrong scope items deleted, 0 completions orphaned), and redone one row at a time so an insert cannot drift from its strategy. The seeder helper already inserts per-row and never had the bug. Compliance moved 86.3 -> 85.2 as the 21 new scope items entered the scheduled denominator with no completions yet; the on-time gap NARROWED 13.3 -> 12.2, so the forward-only ratchet passed and was re-accepted at the tighter ceiling.

AH09.title: Weibull fit - with too few failures, does it refuse or guess?
AH09.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. THE ENGINE'S REFUSAL PATH IS EXCELLENT AND STAYS - recorded as a real result, because the arc's premise (AHK2) half-expected it to be missing. python-api/reliability/weibull.py sets MIN_FAILURES_FOR_FIT=4 and below it attempts NO fit: beta NULL, eta NULL, failure_pattern='insufficient_data', plus a degenerate-likelihood guard for all-identical durations. That is why min(n_failures) across 91 fits is exactly 4 - nothing weaker ever gets a number. It also writes an ACTIONABLE diagnostic: 'Need at least 4 corrective events in the lookback window (have 2). Log more breakdowns or widen since_days before refitting.' THE DEFECT IS THAT THE SENTENCE COULD ONLY EVER BE SEEN ONCE. weibull_fits had no diagnostic column, so persistFit never wrote it, v_weibull_truth could not expose it, and loadLatestWeibull selected a column set that could not contain it - fit.diagnostic was undefined and diagEl.textContent = fit.diagnostic || '' cleared the box. Visible for a few seconds after Compute; blank on every load after that. What a planner opening the asset the next day saw: beta '--', eta '--', a pill reading 'insufficient data', and an EMPTY bordered box where the explanation belongs. The number is correctly absent and the REASON is silently absent too - the F18 dead-card shape landing on the most important sentence in the reliability workbench. FIXED as ONE definition rather than two: the engine already writes the sentence, so persist what it wrote (migration 20260728000014 adds the column and re-exposes the view; the fitter writes it; the page selects it on the LOAD path). Re-deriving the wording client-side would have put the same sentence in two places and let them drift - the logbook arc's three-ways-to-say-'corrective'. A NEAR-MISS OF MY OWN, caught by reading before rewriting: v_weibull_truth is NOT a plain projection - it is DISTINCT ON (hive_id, asset_id, COALESCE(fmea_mode_id,'_')) ORDER BY generated_at DESC, which is what makes it the LATEST fit per asset, and it aliases id AS fit_id. My first migration draft recreated it from the column list alone, which would have silently handed every consumer the FULL fit history and renamed a column. Caught by dumping the real definition first; the gate now asserts the DISTINCT ON survives. AND ONE MORE INSTRUMENT ERROR: my post-migration leak check ran as the postgres superuser (BYPASSRLS) and reported 'LEAK'. Re-run as a real authenticated member: 1 hive visible, 31 rows, no leak. VERIFIED LIVE on a page LOAD (not the compute path): beta '--', eta '--', pattern 'insufficient data', meta 'n_failures 2 - n_censored 1 - window 365d', and the diagnostic now reads in full. GATED by tools/validate_refusal_reason_persists.py (registered), which holds the whole round-trip because breaking any link restores the silent blank; teeth proven twice - reverting the page select and dropping the column each give exit 1.

AH10.title: P-F interval - the number that sets inspection frequency
AH10.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28 - CLEAN, with one measured asymmetry recorded rather than migrated away. The P-F engine refuses properly, with FOUR distinct diagnostics (fewer than 2 valid readings, no detectable P-F pair, and two degenerate cases), and the compute path COMMUNICATES the refusal: #pf-status shows data.diagnostic and the toast says 'No P-F pair detected, see diagnostic.' So unlike AH9, the user is told why at the moment it happens. THE ASYMMETRY, and its cause measured rather than assumed: a P-F refusal has NO ROW AT ALL, so its reason cannot survive a reload the way weibull_fits.diagnostic now does. Verified live on the SAME asset - the Weibull card reads 'insufficient data' with its full reason, while the P-F panel shows only its first-run copy. AND THE STATED REASON WAS WRONG IN BOTH COMMENTS. python-api/reliability/pf_interval.py and supabase/functions/pf-calculator/index.ts each said refusals are not persisted 'because pf_intervals.pf_days has a CHECK > 0'. That is not the blocker: in SQL `NULL > 0` evaluates to NULL and a CHECK treats NULL as SATISFIED, so the CHECK would happily accept a NULL. Probed it - the insert fails 23502, the NOT NULL constraint. The distinction is load-bearing for the next reader: someone relaxing the CHECK to persist refusals would find them still rejected and not know why. Both comments corrected to name the real constraint and to record the consequence. NOT MIGRATED, deliberately: making pf_days nullable to store refusals would weaken a column whose not-nullness is what guarantees every stored P-F row HAS a window - the same reasoning that kept get_pm_compliance_smrp intact in the PM arc. The first-run copy is also correct guidance in the state where it actually appears (this asset has never had a P-F computed); it only reads oddly in the seconds right after a refusal, where #pf-status carries the truth directly beneath it. Recorded as a low-severity nit, not a defect. FMEA RPN is the remaining third of AHK2 and needs a DIFFERENT question - it is arithmetic on three 1-10 inputs, so the issue is whether the inputs are defensible, not whether the product is.

AH11.title: Asset identity: rename propagates to PM + logbook
AH11.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. sync_pm_asset_identity (added by PM3 earlier in this same arc) does its job correctly - and pm_assets is not the only place an asset's identity lives. FOUR other tables key off the asset TAG as free text and none of them moved. MEASURED LIVE renaming GEN-002 -> GEN-002X through the signed-in client: asset_nodes 1, pm_assets 2 synced, and left behind 103 logbook.machine + 12 fault_knowledge.machine + 1 asset_risk_scores pointing at a tag that no longer existed. Platform-wide: logbook 3,739 of 3,811 rows hold a live tag; fault_knowledge 534 of 534 (100%); asset_risk_scores 255 of 259; parts_staging_recommendations 3 of 4. EVERY ONE OF THOSE COLUMNS HOLDS THE TAG - including the two literally named asset_name - so a display-name change is harmless and a TAG change is what breaks them. That distinction decides the whole fix and I only found it by measuring which values the columns actually contain rather than trusting the column names. SEVERITY IS NOT UNIFORM, which is worth recording: logbook is the least severe because 3,739 of 3,811 rows also carry asset_node_id, so the timeline survives by uuid and only the displayed string goes stale (the 72 text-only rows do genuinely sever). fault_knowledge has NO uuid column at all, so a rename severs the AI's learned fault corpus permanently with nothing reporting it. asset_risk_scores is the worst, because the page does not merely lose the score - it ASSERTS something false: the risk card falls back to 'No risk score yet for this asset. Scores are computed daily at 13:00 PHT... a score will appear here.' That sentence is honest about a cold start and a lie about a renamed asset. FIX: sync_asset_identity covers all five in one transaction and returns per-table counts so the caller can report what actually moved; sync_pm_asset_identity stays as a thin wrapper (it is in canonical_registry and logbook.html called it) so the narrow behaviour is no longer reachable even by accident. Plus a MERGE GUARD: renaming onto a tag another asset already holds would fuse two machines' logbook, fault knowledge and risk history with nothing able to separate them again - refused outright, and surfaced to the user via toast, because only they can pick another tag. TWO BUGS IN MY OWN FIX, both caught live, both now gated: (1) The merge guard fired against the asset renaming ITSELF. Callers update asset_nodes.tag FIRST and then ask for propagation, so by the time the RPC runs the new tag is already in use - by the very row being renamed. Added p_node_id to exclude it; logbook.html passes it (its `id` IS the asset_nodes id). (2) FAR WORSE - THE FIX WROTE ACROSS A TENANT BOUNDARY. The first draft scoped its UPDATEs to 'any hive the caller belongs to'. Tags are unique per HIVE, not per platform, and the fixture gives every hive its own GEN-002. Renaming Lucena's asset also rewrote Manila Electronics Assembly's 60 logbook rows, 6 fault_knowledge rows, its risk score, a parts recommendation and a pm_asset. Found because the REVERT leg was refused by another tenant's asset - the false clash was the symptom that exposed the real corruption. Repaired to 0 residual across all three hives, verified per hive. Every UPDATE now carries BOTH hive_id = v_hive AND the membership check: v_hive alone would trust a tag from any tenant, membership alone was the bug. RE-PROVEN with hive scoping: rename moved 50 rows ALL in my hive (43 logbook + 6 fault + 1 pm); the other hive's 60 logbook rows untouched; revert symmetric; final state identical to start, 0 rows on the test tag. GATE validate_asset_identity_spine. Its FIRST version had no teeth on the check that mattered most - it counted '= v_hive' occurrences globally, and deleting the predicate from one UPDATE still cleared the >= 6 threshold because the SELECT INTO and the merge guard also use v_hive. It now slices the migration per UPDATE statement and checks each on its own; teeth re-proven, one deleted predicate -> FAIL on exactly that statement. A counting threshold is not a gate. The live half reports orphan tags (a row naming a tag no asset in its hive carries): 77 pre-existing, 72 of them the logbook rows with no asset_node_id to fall back on.

AH12.title: Delete / retire an asset - what happens to FMEA, RCM, history
AH12.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. THE FK DESIGN IS RIGHT AND IS NOT CHANGED - recorded as a real result. CASCADE covers what is genuinely PART of the asset (rcm_fmea_modes, weibull_fits, pf_intervals, sensor_readings, asset_embeddings, asset_edges) while SET NULL covers records that merely REFERENCE it and stand on their own (logbook, pm_knowledge, anomaly_signals, drone_inspections, and parent_id). A technician's written entry survives the asset being retired - the same disposition PM6 verified for logbook.pm_completion_id. And tg_guard_approval already refuses a non-supervisor deleting an APPROVED node, so the AUTHORITY half was covered. WHAT WAS MISSING IS THE EVIDENCE, and the blast radius is far larger than PM12's. Measured on the worst real node (VFD-001): one DELETE takes 4,331 rows - 4 FMEA modes, 2 RCM strategies, 1 Weibull fit, 1 P-F interval and 4,323 SENSOR READINGS - and orphans 59 logbook entries. Nothing recorded any of it. THE READINGS ARE THE PART THAT MATTERS AND THE PART LEAST OBVIOUS: losing 4,323 of them is not losing a number on a screen, it is losing the ability to EVER re-derive a Weibull fit or a P-F interval for that machine - precisely the numbers AHK2 established decide when it is next opened up. The FMEA and strategies can be re-authored by a person; the condition history cannot. FIXED by migration 20260728000016, the PM12 pattern: a BEFORE DELETE trigger counting the children while they still exist and recording fmea/strategies/weibull/pf/readings destroyed plus logbook entries ORPHANED (a separate word, because those survive - they only lose their link). BEFORE matters: after the cascade the counts no longer exist to record. Proven live in a rolled-back transaction - the audit row reads exactly {fmea 4, strategies 2, weibull 1, pf 1, sensor_readings 4323, logbook_orphaned 59} and the readings really were gone (0 left). GATED as a 7th check in validate_approval_authority; teeth proven by dropping the trigger (exit 1).

AH13.title: Cross-hive: foreign reliability data cannot leak or be written
AH13.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. READS ARE CORRECTLY ISOLATED - 0 rows across all four reliability tables (fmea, strategies, weibull, pf) when read as a member of another hive. Recorded as a real result: this is competitive plant knowledge and the boundary holds. WRITES HAD THE PM13 GAP: the WITH CHECK validates that hive_id is one the caller belongs to and says NOTHING about whether the PARENT lives there. Probed live, both accepted - an FMEA mode with hive_id=MINE and asset_id=ANOTHER HIVE'S node, and a strategy with hive_id=MINE and fmea_mode_id=THEIRS. AN INSTRUMENT ERROR THAT NEARLY BECAME A FALSE 'CLEAN': my first probe came back BLOCKED with 23514 and I almost recorded isolation as holding. 23514 is check_violation, not 42501 - it was rcm_strategies_decision_check rejecting my own invalid enum value ('scheduled_task' is not in the allowed set). The tenancy question was still untested. Re-probed with a valid decision and both writes went through. Verify WHAT blocked it, not merely THAT something did. SEVERITY MEASURED, AND GENUINELY LOWER THAN PM13's: there the injected completion CREDITED the foreign hive (502->503) because get_pm_compliance_smrp joins by scope_item_id regardless of hive. Here every reliability view filters by hive_id, so reading v_fmea_truth AS a member of the target hive returns 0 rows for an injected severity-10 mode. The attacker pollutes their OWN hive with a phantom row pointing at an asset they cannot see. FIXED ANYWAY, and the reason is the point: the containment is CONSUMER-DEPENDENT - it holds only while every reader, current and future, filters by hive_id rather than joining through asset_id or fmea_mode_id. PM13 is the proof of what happens when one RPC does not. Migration 20260728000017 adds a RESTRICTIVE parent-hive WITH CHECK to all four tables. Safe to tighten, measured first: 0 existing rows violate it on any table. Proven: both injections BLOCKED, both legitimate own-hive writes still 1 row. GATED as an 8th check in validate_approval_authority; teeth proven by dropping one of the four guards (exit 1).

AH14.title: Parts staging: accept / dismiss (inherited F43 expires_at)
AH14.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28 - the inherited F43, and it was live on TWO pages. asset-hub SELECTED expires_at and then never used it: not in the filter, not in the render. MEASURED: all 3 recommendations carrying an expiry had already passed it (2026-07-27, the day before this walk) and were still status='pending', so the card rendered them as live and actionable with checkboxes ticked and a 'Stage selected' button. Nothing anywhere expires them - no job, no trigger, no filter - so a recommendation stays pending forever and status='pending' does NOT mean current. WHY IT MATTERS: a parts recommendation is a RISK ASSESSMENT with a shelf life. It says 'given this asset's risk score today, stage these parts'. Acting on an expired one means committing stock against a model run the system itself already declared stale. alert-hub had the SAME bug and worse - its query did not even SELECT expires_at, so expired recommendations sat in the 'what needs attention now' feed. TWO DIFFERENT DISPOSITIONS, deliberately: asset-hub KEEPS the card and marks it expired (this is the asset's own page, where 'a recommendation was made and went stale' explains why there is nothing to act on - the false affordance is removed, not the information); alert-hub FILTERS it out (a stale risk assessment there is not context, it is noise competing with real alerts). AND THE DISABLED BUTTON IS NOT THE GUARD. A UI-only gate is bypassable (feedback_ui_only_approval_gate_is_bypassable), and there is a second reason to re-check: a card left open on screen can cross its own expiry while the user reads it. _onStagingAccept re-tests expires_at against the clock at the moment of the write. VERIFIED LIVE on AC-002: note reads 'This recommendation expired 23h ago and is no longer safe to act on...', Accept disabled and relabelled 'Expired', all 3 checkboxes disabled, Dismiss still enabled (clearing a stale card is exactly what a planner should be able to do). BYPASS ATTEMPTED AND REFUSED: force-enabling the button and its checkboxes then calling the handler produced 'That recommendation has expired' and parts_staged_reservations stayed at 1 - no write. alert-hub: 2 pending -> 1 after the filter, and the feed now carries exactly one staging item, the non-expired one. A NULL expires_at is correctly KEPT on both surfaces - no expiry set means no shelf life was declared, which is not the same as expired.

AH15.title: Asset Brain Q&A - citations are checkable (inherited F41)
AH15.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28 - the inherited F41, and it had TWO halves, only one of which was obvious. THE VISIBLE HALF: the model returns { kind, index } and the page rendered it literally - 'Sources: logbook #1, fmea #3'. That index points into an array the EDGE FUNCTION assembled and the page has never seen, so the single thing a citation exists for - letting a reader verify the claim - was impossible. Provenance rendered as internals, which is exactly feedback_provenance_user_voice_not_internals. THE HALF THAT MAKES IT A CORRECTNESS BUG, NOT A UX ONE: an index PAST THE END of the array rendered identically to a real one. If the model cited 'logbook #7' when only 5 entries were supplied, the reader saw a confident, plausible source for a sentence nothing supports. A FABRICATED citation was indistinguishable from a grounded one - and grounding is the entire product claim of an Asset Brain. Nothing validated the index anywhere in the chain. FIXED WHERE THE CONTEXT ACTUALLY LIVES: resolveCitations() in asset-brain-query maps each {kind,index} against the arrays that function built and returns a human-readable label plus resolved:true|false. All ten kinds covered (logbook, pm, neighbor, similar, fmea, rcm, pf, risk-factor, and the singletons weibull/risk/stat), duplicates collapsed (the same source cited twice adds no evidence and reads as two), kind/index preserved for any existing consumer. UNRESOLVED ONES ARE SHOWN, NOT DROPPED: an answer leaning on a source that does not exist is the most important thing to know about it, and silently filtering them would restore the original invisibility under a nicer surface. And no citations AT ALL now says so explicitly rather than rendering an empty line. VERIFIED LIVE, twice over. Direct edge invoke on WLD-001 returned resolved labels: 'FMEA - MCCB trip unit drift (RPN 168)'. Then a real Ask through the PAGE's own handler (which routes via ai-gateway, so this also proves the structured passthrough preserves the new fields) rendered: 'Based on: FMEA - MCCB trip unit drift (RPN 168) / FMEA - Switch-mode PSU output ripple (RPN 150) / FMEA - Cable insulation breakdown (RPN 108) / Weibull fit - wearout (beta 3.59, eta 165 d) / P-F interval - temperature_c - inspect every 6 d'. Every one of those is checkable against the asset's own records in seconds. All four surface states exercised: all-resolved, mixed, all-unresolved, and none. INSTRUMENT NOTE: the four-state check ran a COPY of the page's render logic, so the real proof of the page path is the live Ask above, not that simulation - which is why I ran it.

AH16.title: Telemetry / sensor panel with and without data
AH16.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. THE HEADLINE: v_sensor_truth.is_anomaly was defined as quality_flag = 'ANOMALY', and the sensor_readings CHECK allows only good|uncertain|bad|stale. The database FORBADE the one value that would make the flag true - false for all 77,814 readings and always would be, so this is dead by construction, not a fixture gap a reseed fixes. FOUR SURFACES were built on it and none had ever fired: asset-hub's #sensor-anomaly-banner (added in Tier4.4 expressly to close the 'anomaly buried in the per-parameter Z-score chip' gap - so that gap stayed open the whole time; measured live on RC-001, the chip read ANOMALY 4.5-sigma while the banner above it stayed hidden), index.html's Today's One Thing ranker, the get_hive_dashboard RPC, and the Companion source registry. A Playwright parity spec asserts on it and PASSES, because 0 = 0. And formula_contracts.json z_score_anomaly_3sigma claimed since 2026-05-20 that sensor-readings-ingest sets it - that string appears nowhere in the function. Three layers each assuming another did the work. FIX, and why not just widen the CHECK: quality_flag is a DATA-QUALITY field (is this reading trustworthy?); an anomaly is a different claim (the reading is trustworthy AND the machine is behaving oddly). Folding ANOMALY into that enum would make a stale sensor and a failing bearing raise the same flag. So mig ...018 gives the anomaly its own boolean column + partial index, the view keeps its exact column name and position (every consumer untouched, they simply start seeing true), the ingest fn got the z-score writer that was documented but never built, and the contract now describes what exists. Baseline discipline in the writer: incoming rows are judged against history that PRECEDES them, so a batch of identical faulty readings cannot establish its own normal; under 12 samples or zero variance it flags nothing rather than guessing; and a failed baseline pass never drops a bridge's readings. LIVE-PROVEN end to end through the real edge function, not simulated: posted 2 normal vibration readings and one 7.4-sigma outlier -> {inserted:3, anomalies:1}, only the outlier flagged, and the banner rendered for the first time in the platform's life: 'vibration reading 3-sigma off baseline / Latest anomaly at Jul 28, 2026, 11:37 AM. Value: 14.8.' SECOND DEFECT - the telemetry footer claimed the window: it read '500 reading(s) in the last 30 days' for an asset with 3,174, because rows.length IS the .limit(500). Worse than AH5's silent fleet cap, since the number is stated as a fact about the window while every mean, range and sigma above it came from that truncated slice - measured, the sample spans 3.5 days, not 30, so a month-long drift reads as normal. Now: 'latest 500 of 3,174 readings in the last 30 days - the figures above describe this most-recent sample, not the whole window', and each parameter line carries its actual span (n=167 over 3.5 d). Under-cap path proven unchanged at 120 rows by stubbing the query. MY OWN NEAR-MISS, caught by the file-memory hook: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW does NOT carry reloptions forward - my first apply WIPED security_invoker (pg_class.reloptions went NULL), which would have made a canonical read bypass sensor_readings RLS into a cross-hive leak. Restored, restated in the migration with a comment, and validate_truth_view_security_invoker.py (which already existed) confirms all v_*_truth views green. The seeder also stopped writing anomaly bursts as quality_flag='uncertain', which was the same conflation in fixture form.

AH17.title: External CMMS ids - the dead card (inherited F18)
AH17.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28 - the inherited F18 confirmed, and it was broken TWICE over, which is why it read as one vague 'KEEP-or-CUT' item in the PDDA backlog. (1) THE READ: loadDetailExternalIds does `_allNodes.find(...).external_ids`, but the fleet select at the top of the page omitted external_ids from its column list. So node.external_ids was ALWAYS undefined, keys.length was always 0, and #ext-card hid itself on every asset in the fleet - a card that could never render, on any row, ever. One word in the select is the whole read-side fix. (2) THE DATA: external_ids was populated on 0 of 95 nodes, so even with the select fixed there was nothing to show. That is AHK3 a fourth time - and it explains why nobody could tell whether the card was broken or just empty. Seeded a SAMPLE (~20%, now 16 of 95) and co-landed _external_ids_sample in asset_brain.py, because a plant that has never run a CMMS import legitimately has none and BOTH states must exist. VERIFIED LIVE on PB-001: the card renders 'Fiix FX000074 - SAP_PM EQ-PB001'. The KEEP-or-CUT question the backlog left open is answered by keeping it: the feature works, it just had no read path and no data. NOT MINE, recorded rather than swept up: the page logs a 401 on analytics_events with 'JWT issued at future' - clock skew between the local container and the host, handled gracefully by utils.js (it warns and continues). Environmental, not a page defect.

AH18.title: Mobile 390px at-the-asset lookup (QR -> detail)
AH18.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28 at a TRUE 390px, via the QR path (?tag=WLD-001) rather than a node_id, because that is the link the printed tag on the machine actually encodes. INSTRUMENT FIRST, per feedback_browser_resize_lies_check_innerwidth: browser_resize(390) would have given 585 at this display's dpr 0.667, making every measurement 1.5x wrong. Resized to 260 and ECHOED window.innerWidth = 390 before measuring anything. WHAT HELD: no horizontal overflow anywhere (documentElement.scrollWidth 367 < 390), and zero overflowing elements inside #detail-view. The initial sweep flagged 8 'overflowing' nodes, but reading them showed they were the closed slide-out feedback drawer and the search overlay, both positioned off-screen BY DESIGN - a raw right>innerWidth test does not distinguish 'broken layout' from 'deliberately parked off-canvas', so each one had to be looked at rather than counted. FOUND: 'Print QR tag' (104x36) and 'View alerts' (110x36) were the only two controls in the whole detail view under 44px - every other action on the page was already 44. And they are precisely the two the at-the-asset journey reaches for: a worker standing at the machine, gloved, having just scanned the tag, wants the alerts or a replacement tag. 36px is the wrong size for exactly that context, and the fact that these two are the page's most MOBILE-specific actions while the desk-bound ones were already compliant is the tell that they were added without a 390 walk. Raised both to 44. Re-measured: all 22 visible controls in the detail view now >= 44px. EVERY ELEMENT THIS ARC ADDED re-measured at 390 with zero overflow: the AP pill (41x20, leading each FMEA row as intended), the FMEA row head (271 wide, wrapping cleanly), the telemetry sample footer, the fleet cap note, the staging expiry note, the CMMS sync line ('Last synced from Fiix at 5d ago (active)', 301 wide) and the citations list. FULL-PAGE screenshot taken and read top to bottom, not a viewport crop - the Whole-Artifact Discipline, since everything below the fold is exactly where a mobile regression hides. Header, risk profile, Reliability Workbench with all three AP-ordered FMEA rows, Live Telemetry, Timeline, External Systems and the Ask box all render within the 367px content width with nothing clipped.

AHK1.name: A governance decision needs an IDENTITY, not a name
AHK1.notes: OPEN on measured evidence (2026-07-28 ground). asset_nodes carries submitted_by and approved_by as TEXT while 0 of 95 rows have auth_uid at all, and the table has 0 audit triggers. So an approval - the governance act the whole queue exists for - is attributed to a typed NAME, recorded nowhere the database can vouch for, and performed on rows nobody is provably the author of. Distinct from PMK3, which covered a COMPLETION's tamper-evidence: this is the DECISION itself, plus the forgeable-name half PMK3 never had to face because pm_completions has a real auth_uid. REFINED BY THE AH3 WALK, which is what a walk is for. The premise was half wrong and the correction is worth more than the guess: the approval ACT is NOT ungoverned - wh_guard_supervisor_approval enforces it at the database across six tables. What was missing was the OTHER outcome. Approving and refusing are the same authority exercised two ways, and the guard recognised only the first, so a submitter could reject their own work and write the reviewer's explanation. Fixed + gated (see AH03). SWEEP PARTIAL - two halves of the original premise remain and are stated rather than quietly closed: (1) submitted_by and approved_by are still TEXT names, not identity FKs, so attribution is forgeable even where the ACT is now gated; (2) asset_nodes / rcm_strategies / rcm_fmea_modes still carry 0 audit triggers across 567 rows, so an approval decision leaves no database record - the PMK3 shape on a governance act rather than a completion. SWEEP CLOSED 2026-07-28, and BOTH remaining halves turned out differently than the class premise said - which is the second time this arc a walk corrected it, and the corrections are the value. HALF ONE, THE NAMES: the premise was that submitted_by and approved_by are forgeable TEXT. They are NOT. bind_asset_nodes_submitter (BEFORE INSERT) sets auth_uid := auth.uid() and overwrites worker_name and submitted_by from hive_members; bind_approved_by_from_hive overwrites approved_by from the session whenever it changes. Caught by accident: a probe deliberately wrote approved_by='Someone Else' and the row came back 'Leandro Marquez'. So the platform already binds identity server-side on both. The SUBTLETY worth keeping, and why 20260728000013 was still needed: bind_approved_by_from_hive only fires when approved_by CHANGES. In AH3's hole the worker rejected by setting status + rejection_reason ALONE, leaving approved_by untouched - so the binding trigger had nothing to bind and the row showed a rejection with no approver and a worker-written reason. Server-side name-binding does not cover a field the attacker simply does not touch. HALF TWO, THE RECORD: this one was real. 83 asset_nodes sat in a decided state and ZERO decisions were recorded - the 11 approve/reject rows in hive_audit_log were all CLIENT-written and none were for assets. A client-written row is skipped by any write that bypasses the page, which AH3 proved reachable. Closed by migration 20260728000015: an AFTER UPDATE trigger firing only on a transition INTO a reviewer state, recording status_was/now, the rejection_reason, submitted_by, the claimed approved_by AND the identity resolved from auth.uid() - kept as separate fields so a mismatch between the claimed approver and the actual writer is visible rather than silently reconciled. Scoped so an ordinary edit to an approved asset stays out of the trail, keeping it readable enough to audit. Proven: a location edit logs 0 rows, the reject decision logs 1 with the full picture. THE CLASS AS IT NOW STANDS: a governance decision needs (a) an identity bound where the write lands - already true here, (b) an authority check covering EVERY outcome, not just approval - fixed in AH3, and (c) a database record of the decision itself - fixed here. Gated by tools/validate_approval_authority.py, now 6 checks; teeth proven by dropping the audit trigger (exit 1) and against the real pre-fix guard (3 of 4 fail).

AHK2.name: A number that sets inspection timing must be FALSIFIABLE
AHK2.notes: OPEN on measured evidence. Weibull beta/eta, the P-F interval and FMEA RPN each DECIDE WHEN A MACHINE IS NEXT OPENED UP - they do not report history, they set future action, so being wrong is physical rather than cosmetic. Ground measured 172 RCM strategies and 300 FMEA modes, all approved, computed by edge functions (weibull-fitter, pf-calculator) with no in-repo oracle found. Each needs a stated method, a REFUSAL path when the data cannot support the fit, and a checkable oracle. Distinct from PMK1: that was a metric flattering what was DONE; this is a computed value deciding what happens NEXT. REFINED BY THE AH9 WALK. The premise was that these numbers might be produced without a refusal path; the measurement says otherwise and the correction is the finding. Weibull HAS a well-designed refusal (MIN_FAILURES_FOR_FIT=4, no fit attempted, an actionable diagnostic) and it is the honest kind - it declines rather than guessing. What was broken is the DURABILITY of the refusal's reason: computed, returned once, never stored, so the explanation was blank on every page load after the first. A calculation that refuses is only as useful as the sentence that survives with it. SWEEP PARTIAL, stated rather than quietly closed: the P-F interval calculator (pf_intervals, 91 rows) has the same shape and is UNWALKED - whether it refuses on thin data, and whether ITS reason persists, is AH10 and the next slice. FMEA RPN (300 modes) is arithmetic on three 1-10 inputs and needs a different question - whether the inputs are defensible, not whether the product is. SWEEP CLOSED by AH10 across both computed numbers. Weibull: refuses well AND its reason now persists (fixed + gated). P-F: refuses well and communicates at compute time, but its reason cannot persist because pf_days is NOT NULL - measured, and deliberately left that way rather than weakening the column that guarantees every stored P-F row has a real window. The class's rule stands with a caveat worth keeping: a refusal's reason should persist WHERE A ROW EXISTS TO CARRY IT; where the schema legitimately forbids the row, the refusal must at least be unmistakable at the moment it happens, which P-F does. RPN is arithmetic on human 1-10 inputs and belongs to a different question (are the inputs defensible), noted on AH07.

AHK3.name: The fixture must contain every state the workflow can be in
AHK3.notes: EARNED BY THE AH2 WALK 2026-07-28, and it earned itself by BLOCKING one. RULE: a workflow state with no rows is a state nobody has walked, so the seeder is part of the test surface - and the failure is quiet, because a fixture missing a STATE looks exactly like a fixture that is fine. EVIDENCE: asset_nodes had 95 rows, ALL status='approved', 0 pending, 0 rejected, 0 with auth_uid. Every affordance built for the other states - the pending queue, the rejection reason, the restore path - was unreachable, which is why the PDDA arc's F21 (a worker's Pending-assets tile always reads 0) sat undiagnosed: there had never been a pending asset to see. The hole in AH3 had been sitting behind that same gap. SHARPENS LB13/LB17 from missing RELATIONSHIPS to missing STATES. FIX: the seeder now generates status and its companion fields together (_governance_state), so the states exist AND cannot be internally incoherent. SWEEP PARTIAL: rcm_strategies is still 172 approved / 0 unapproved, so the strategy approval gate remains unwalkable - that is AH8's fixture and the next slice. GATE TODO: a check that each governed table holds >0 rows in every non-terminal state it defines. SWEEP CLOSED by AH8: rcm_strategies now carries its non-terminal state (146/26) and the strategy->PM link has both branches (21 linked / 151 cold-start). Three tables were missing a state for three DIFFERENT reasons - asset_nodes because a seeder hand-off dropped the field, rcm_strategies because an approval flag was unconditional, and the PM link because the empty state was DELIBERATE and nobody had seeded its counterpart. The last is the subtle one: a documented, correct disposition can still leave a branch undemonstrable, and the answer is a SAMPLE rather than overriding the disposition. GATE CLOSED: tools/validate_workflow_states_present.py holds six states open across the three tables this arc found empty, so a future seeder change cannot quietly re-close a branch. It asserts REPRESENTATION rather than a ratio - the point is never the proportion, it is that the next walk has something to walk. Teeth proven by emptying one state (exit 1).
